intro: Looking for a charity bookkeeper near you usually means you're helping run a small charity, community group or social enterprise and you want someone local who understands how charity money has to be handled. Charities deal with restricted and unrestricted funds, donations and Gift Aid in ways that ordinary business bookkeeping doesn't cover, so it helps to find someone who does this kind of work regularly. We can introduce you to a suitable UK bookkeeper, who will discuss your needs and quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a charity bookkeeper usually need
need_lead: Most people searching this way are trustees, treasurers or volunteers who need steady, accurate help with charity finances rather than general business bookkeeping.
needs: You're a trustee or treasurer of a small charity and the books have fallen behind, so you need someone to bring them up to date.
Your charity receives donations that are restricted to a particular purpose, and you need those funds tracked separately from general money.
You want Gift Aid declarations kept in good order and the claims handled correctly, without missing paperwork.
Your trustees need clear, regular reports so they can see how the charity is doing and make decisions with confidence.
You're approaching an independent examination and want the records tidy and ready before that happens.
context: Charity bookkeeping isn't just ordinary bookkeeping with a different label. Charities have to separate restricted funds, given for a specific purpose, from unrestricted funds, and keep a clear record of donations and Gift Aid so the picture is accurate for trustees and for independent examination. A bookkeeper who works with charities will understand this from the start.

Bookkeeping isn't a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Describe the kind of charity or group you run and roughly what it does, so we can match you with someone familiar with similar work.
Explain whether you have restricted funds, and how many different funds you need to keep separate.
Mention whether Gift Aid is involved and whether declarations are already in place or need sorting out.
Say where your records currently stand, for example whether they're up to date, behind, or being started from scratch.
Let us know what your trustees need from the bookkeeping, such as regular reports or preparation for independent examination.
Tell us where you're based and whether you'd prefer someone local or are happy to work remotely.
questions: How do you handle restricted and unrestricted funds in your bookkeeping?
What experience do you have with Gift Aid declarations and claims?
Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice?
What reports would you give our trustees, and how often would they receive them?

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper handle restricted and unrestricted funds for our charity?
faqs.a: Yes, a bookkeeper who works with charities will keep restricted and unrestricted funds separate so your records show clearly what each pot of money is for. It's worth asking about this directly, because it's central to charity bookkeeping.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help with Gift Aid?
faqs.a: A charity bookkeeper can keep your Gift Aid declarations organised and help make sure the records behind claims are in order. They'll be clear about what falls within bookkeeping and what needs an accountant.

faqs.q: Do we need a bookkeeper who is near us?
faqs.a: Many charities prefer someone local for convenience, but much bookkeeping can be done remotely if that suits you better. When you enquire, tell us which you'd prefer and we'll take it into account.

faqs.q: What should we have ready before we speak to a bookkeeper?
faqs.a: It helps to have your current records, any Gift Aid declarations and a rough idea of the funds you hold. The bookkeeper can then tell you what they need and quote you directly.
